articles.title: “That was my biggest goal in life”: How Angel Reese turned her first WNBA home into a $1.45M property after a $1.28M purchase in Illinois after her move
articles.summary: International Sports News: Angel Reese’s first WNBA home is back on the market for $1.45 million, more than a year after she purchased the Lemont, Illinois, property for $1.28 m.
articles.body: Angel Reese’s first WNBA home is back on the market for $1.45 million, more than a year after she purchased the Lemont, Illinois, property for $1.28 million. The five-bedroom home became part of Reese’s story shortly after she entered the WNBA, when homeownership was one of the milestones she celebrated alongside a much bigger family goal.The latest listing comes after Reese’s move from the Chicago Sky to the Atlanta Dream and during a season in which she has added several major WNBA records to her name. The property, which was first reported as heading for a $1.45 million listing in June, has since returned to the market in September.Angel Reese’s “Retire My Momma” goal was tied to a bigger family milestoneReese’s Lemont home was more than her first major property purchase. Around the same period, she had already achieved a personal goal involving her mother, Angel Webb Reese.In January 2025, Reese surprised her mother during an episode of her Unapologetically Angel show by revealing that she had paid off her mortgage. Reese told her mother she could retire if she wanted.“Before we sing ‘Happy Birthday,’ you said that if your mortgage was paid off that you would retire or you won't work,” Reese said during the surprise. “You can pick if you want to work still, your mortgage today has been paid.”Reese later explained just how important the gesture was to her.“That was my biggest goal in life to retire you and pay your mortgage or whatever you wanted not to work,” she told her mother. Reese also added, “You're a hard-working woman, you don't need me for no money. That's why I always say, ‘She never needed me for no money.’”Her mother, who was visibly emotional during the surprise, responded, “Are you serious?” Reese then told her that the mortgage had been taken care of and that she could continue working if she wanted.Just a few months later, Reese reached another personal milestone by buying her own home.When she celebrated the purchase on X, she posted green check emojis beside two goals: “retire my momma” and “become a homeowner.” The post came with a photo of Reese celebrating the new property.That connection gives the Lemont property a personal backstory. Reese was not simply celebrating a new house. She was also highlighting a period in which helping her mother financially and building her own future were both major goals.The home itself is located at 12735 Caruso Court on a 0.41-acre lot. Reese bought it in April 2025 through a limited liability company, according to county records.The 3,600-square-foot property has five bedrooms and three bathrooms. Its features include an open-concept design, a great room near the chef’s kitchen, custom window treatments and updated lighting.There is also a first-floor study, an entertainment room, a three-car garage, a lookout basement and a fully fenced backyard. One of the bathrooms includes a freestanding tub and a walk-in shower.Reese paid $1.28 million for the home. The current $1.45 million asking price is roughly $170,000 higher than the purchase price, although the listing price does not mean the property has sold for that amount.Her Chicago-to-Atlanta move came during a record-setting WNBA seasonThe home listing follows one of the biggest changes in Reese’s professional career.The Chicago Sky selected the 6-foot-4 forward with the seventh overall pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft. After two seasons in Chicago, Reese was traded to the Atlanta Dream in April 2026. The deal included Atlanta’s first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, while the teams also agreed to swap second-round picks in 2028.Her first season in Atlanta has since produced a long list of individual milestones.In August, Reese was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week after averaging 24 points, 11.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 3.7 steals across three games. She followed that with another Player of the Week award in early September.During that second stretch, Reese grabbed a WNBA-record 26 rebounds against the Los Angeles Sparks. She also passed A’ja Wilson’s previous single-season rebounding record of 451. Against the Minnesota Lynx, Reese recorded her 29th double-double of the season, setting a new WNBA single-season record.She then joined Team USA for the 2026 FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup in Germany. The United States won the tournament, giving Reese another international gold medal to add to her résumé.After returning to Atlanta, Reese wasted little time making another entry in the record book.On Sept. 17, she scored 30 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in only 25 minutes as the Dream defeated the Connecticut Sun 103-59. She shot 11-of-14 from the field and recorded her 30th double-double of the season, extending her own WNBA single-season record.Reese also became the first player in WNBA history to record at least 30 points and 10 rebounds while playing 25 minutes or fewer. After the game, she explained her approach following the long break for the World Cup.“I was joking in the locker room that I'm very well-rested, and I was ready to play today,” Reese said. She added, “Right now, it's important to make sure we're setting the tone and leaving a taste in everybody's mouth about what the playoffs are going to look like.”That latest performance came nearly 18 months after Reese bought the Lemont property. The home was purchased soon after she entered the WNBA and celebrated two goals that were deeply personal to her: becoming a homeowner and helping her mother.Now, after a trade to Atlanta, a World Cup gold medal and a record-setting WNBA season, Reese’s first professional home is back on the market with a $1.45 million asking price.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I'm hoping for gold': Star golfer Khalin Joshi backs India’s Asian Games golf teams for medal success
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: With the Asian Games beginning in Japan's Aichi-Nagoya, golfer Khalin Joshi has backed India's men's and women's golf teams to challenge fo.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With the Asian Games beginning in Japan's Aichi-Nagoya, golfer Khalin Joshi has backed India's men's and women's golf teams to challenge for medals.The men's squad features in-form professionals who have excelled both domestically and on the DP World Tour, while the women's team boasts experienced international campaigners.“We have a great team. Yuvraj has been playing excellent golf in Europe, Saptak is leading the Order of Merit, and all of them are riding high on confidence,” he said.“I'm really hopeful they're going to contend. I'm hoping for gold, and I just hope both the men's and women's teams keep the Indian flag flying high.”Joshi insists there has been no dramatic swing change, no new coach and no technical overhaul behind one of the ost consistent spells of his season. The Bengaluru golfer believes the biggest transformation has happened where scores are often decided in the mind.Fresh off his victory at the Nava Raipur Open on Friday, Joshi said “I haven't changed anything much, to be honest. I've just tried to work on my mental game and stay more in the present throughout the round.”That approach proved crucial in Raipur, where relentless rain forced officials to shorten the event to 36 holes. With only nine holes played on each of the final two days, golfers had little room for recovery, making fast starts essential.Rather than playing conservatively, Joshi embraced the conditions. “The moment we heard it was reduced to 36 holes, we knew we had to start from the get-go. Everyone had limited holes, so my mindset was to be aggressive,” he said.“The course was soft, which actually favoured attacking golf. You could hit your numbers and be more aggressive towards the flags.”The win comes at a time when Indian professional golf is enjoying unprecedented depth. Nearly every PGTI event this season has produced tightly contested leaderboards, with established names and emerging youngsters regularly challenging for titles.Joshi believes the increasing prize money and professionalism of the domestic circuit have fundamentally changed the competitive landscape. “The PGTI is very competitive now. We're very top-heavy and the top 20 to 25 players can win on any given week,” he said.He pointed to the current form of golfers including Saptak Talwar, Rashid Khan, Honey Baisoya, Akshay Sharma, Om Prakash Chouhan, Viraj Madappa, Kartik Singh, Kritish Batra and Shubham Jaglan as evidence of the circuit's strength. “People are working harder in the gym and on the golf course. Golf in India is growing by leaps and bounds, and it's only a matter of time before we see many more Indians succeeding internationally.”While technical preparation remains important, Joshi's tournament routine is deliberately uncomplicated. The 33-year-old avoids adding pressure before decisive rounds and instead focuses on slowing everything down. “I sleep well before tournaments and try not to rush anything in the morning,” he said. “I give myself ample time for breakfast, warming up and getting to the tee. Whenever I hurry, things start going haywire. The key for me is to stay slow and just breeze into the first tee.”Interestingly, Joshi says he learns as much from conversations with contemporaries as from senior professionals. Among those he frequently discusses golf with is close friend and DP World Tour regular Shubhankar Sharma. “Shubhankar is a really good friend. We talk regularly about our games and what we're feeling,” Joshi revealed. “Honestly, I try to learn from everybody. It can be a senior player or even a youngster everyone has something valuable to offer.”That openness extends to the increasingly close-knit atmosphere on the Indian tour, where fierce competition coexists with genuine camaraderie.Joshi believes that culture, combined with rising financial opportunities, is inspiring more young golfers to treat the sport as a viable profession.The Raipur champion has little time to celebrate. He returns to action this week at his home course, the Karnataka Golf Association, before a week's break ahead of the Tour Championship at Jaypee Greens and the lucrative DP World India Championship from Oct 15-18 at the Delhi Golf Club where only the top 24 players on the Order of Merit will tee up.For a golfer whose biggest victory this season was built on quieting the mind, the objective remains unchanged. “Just stay present everything else takes care of itself.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India’s Hockey teams set for Asian Games in white despite promise of blue jerseys
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NAGOYA: At the send-off ceremony for the Indian contingent, Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey had sought to put the jersey controversy to rest.“For .
articles.body: NAGOYA: At the send-off ceremony for the Indian contingent, Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey had sought to put the jersey controversy to rest.“For the Games, the team will wear blue. That’s the primary colour. There’s no confusion, everything is clear,” he had said. But when the Indian men and women take the field against Indonesia and Uzbekistan, respectively, the primary colour may well be white.In the build-up to the FIH World Cup, the Indian teams’ jerseys had come in for sharp criticism after they moved away from the iconic blue and opted for saffron. The switch was attributed to a ‘scientific’ reason — better sighting of the ball — but it made little difference to the men’s side, who finished a disappointing eighth.At the Asian Games, the promised return to blue has proved more complicated. While Tirkey confidently announced that the teams would be back in their traditional colour, he realised only later that the predominant colour of India’s first-choice jersey was actually white, with light blue on the shoulders and neck, and splashes of gold and orange on the front. The shorts and skirts are also in a lighter shade of blue. The second-choice kit is saffron.“All kits for the Asian Games are routed through the IOA and, by the president’s admission, blue was the colour suggested by Hockey India. But the shade of blue and how it is used is up for debate,” a source said.The choice of colour reportedly did not go down well with Tirkey, prompting an effort to get new kits made.“Given how controversy-plagued Hockey India has been over the past few months, the president does not want the focus to shift away from the teams. That’s why he tried very hard to get new sets of jerseys. But given that they have to come through the sponsors, and the women’s team left soon after the send-off, it was always going to be a race against time,” the source said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Suchika Tariyal scripts history, assures India of first Asian Games medal in MMA debut
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India's Suchika Tariyal secured the country's first medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after defeating Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2-0 in the .
articles.body: India's Suchika Tariyal secured the country's first medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after defeating Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2-0 in the women's Traditional Mixed Martial Arts 60kg quarterfinal on Sunday.The 36-year-old produced a composed performance to book her place in the semifinals, where she will compete on Monday. With both losing semifinalists guaranteed bronze medals, Tariyal's progression into the last four ensures India will return from the event with a medal.The achievement is particularly significant as MMA is making its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya 2026.Tariyal's latest success adds another chapter to an unusual combat sports journey that has taken her across several disciplines. She represented India in judo at the 2022 Commonwealth Games before competing in kurash at the 2023 Asian Games. In 2024, she also became a Jiu-Jitsu world champion.Having stepped away from competitive sport, Tariyal eventually returned after encouragement from friends. She opted to take up MMA and began another chapter in her career, overcoming several challenges along the way, including a knee injury, to earn her place in India's Asian Games contingent.Her quarterfinal against Baigalmaa saw Tariyal maintain control as she secured a 2-0 victory. The Mongolian, ranked 92nd in the Eurasia region, was unable to prevent the experienced Indian from advancing to the semifinals.Tariyal will now have an opportunity to add to her medal tally when she takes the mat again on Monday. Regardless of the outcome in the semifinals, her run has already delivered India its first medal of the Aichi-Nagoya Games.For a competitor who has moved between judo, kurash, jiu-jitsu and MMA, the medal is another milestone in a career defined by transitions across combat sports. Her Asian Games debut in MMA has now guaranteed her a place on the podium.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Notre Dame Dominates Second Half to Beat Michigan State
articles.summary: No. 3 Notre Dame stayed perfect Saturday night. The Fighting Irish defeated Michigan State 27-10 at Notre Dame Stadium, improving to 3-0 on the season while...
articles.body:
No. 3 Notre Dame stayed perfect Saturday night.

The Fighting Irish defeated Michigan State 27-10 at Notre Dame Stadium, improving to 3-0 on the season while handing the Spartans their first loss of the year.

The Irish wasted little time getting on the scoreboard.

CJ Carr connected on a 61-yard pass on Notre Dame's first offensive play, immediately putting the Michigan State defense under pressure. The Spartans managed to keep the Irish out of the end zone on that drive, but Notre Dame settled for a field goal.

Notre Dame eventually found the end zone when Nolan James Jr. scored on a two-yard touchdown run, giving the Irish a 10-0 advantage.

Michigan State refused to let the game get away.

The Spartans' offense began finding some rhythm, and quarterback Alessio Milivojevic delivered several impressive throws. Cam Fancher eventually broke through with a 15-yard touchdown run, cutting Notre Dame's lead to 17-10 before halftime.

Michigan State's defense also came up with some important plays, including an interception and a fourth-down stop on a Notre Dame fake punt.

Notre Dame regained control in the second half.

Spencer Porath added a 35-yard field goal in the third quarter before Carr put the game away with a three-yard rushing touchdown early in the fourth. The Irish defense then kept Michigan State from mounting another comeback.

Notre Dame finished with 395 total yards, including 234 through the air and 161 on the ground. Michigan State managed just 167 total yards and turned the ball over twice.

The victory keeps Notre Dame undefeated heading into the rest of its schedule.

Michigan State falls to 2-1 after opening the season with wins over Toledo and Eastern Michigan. Despite the loss, the Spartans showed plenty of fight against one of the nation's top-ranked teams.

For Notre Dame, however, the message was clear.

The Fighting Irish are 3-0, and their defense and physicality continue to make them a major force early in the season.

articles.title: Red Pawns, Red Soldiers: How the Bolsheviks built a chess superpower
articles.summary: Chess News: The latest Chess Olympiad began in Samarkand, a historic city in Uzbekistan, this week. Uzbekistan has been making huge strides in chess. The current .
articles.body: The latest Chess Olympiad began in Samarkand, a historic city in Uzbekistan, this week. Uzbekistan has been making huge strides in chess. The current challenger to D. Gukesh's world championship title is Javokhir Sindarov, a young phenom from Uzbekistan. Uzbekistan won gold in the 2022 Olympiad in Chennai. It is also no coincidence that Uzbekistan was once a Soviet republic like many other modern powerhouse nations in chess.The erstwhile Soviet Union entered the Chess Olympiad for the first time in 1952 in Helsinki and won it. Between its first appearance in 1952 and final appearance in 1990, it participated in nineteen Olympiads and won eighteen while finishing second in the lone Olympiad it did not win.After the collapse of the USSR, Russia won the next six Olympiads in succession between 1992 and 2002. Ukraine and Armenia, earlier part of the Soviet Union, won the next five Olympiads between 2004 and 2012 (while Russia finished second in three out of those five). Uzbekistan won it in 2022. It is an extraordinary record for a game that did not originate in Russia.The seeds of this dominance were laid a century ago in the aftermath of the Bolshevik Revolution. Chess had a respectable history in imperial Russia. It was played by Tsarist aristocrats and members of the urban intelligentsia; Leo Tolstoy was an enthusiast.While the Bolsheviks dismantled much of what existed in the Tsarist regime, including its cultural symbols, they actively promoted chess and appropriated it as a tool in their vision of building a new nation.Chess as a tool to build the New Soviet Man'Alexander Ilyin-Zhenevsky, an unusual combination of chess master, revolutionary and military official, helped bring that vision to fruition. During the Civil War, he worked with Vsevobuch, the system of universal military training created by the new government. Ilyin-Zhenevsky believed that chess could train qualities useful to a soldier: cold nerves, long-range foresight, dynamic decisions under pressure, and iron discipline.The idea found a receptive audience. In October 1920, sixteen of the country's strongest players assembled in Moscow for the All-Russian Chess Olympiad organized by Vsevobuch. The nascent post-revolution Soviet state was dealing with severe food shortages, and it was expected that the tournament participants would get generous rations from the military. However, with playing conditions apparently poor, the players were nearly struck over inadequate food.Ilyin-Zhenevsky later recalled that seven players signed a petition threatening to strike unless the food improved and a cigarette ration was added. Alexander Alekhine, who won the tournament and would later be counted as the first Soviet chess champion, did not sign the petition but said he would stand with those players, because he didn't think it right to play against hungry opponents.Alekhine married a Swiss woman and left Soviet Russia in 1921. He spent the rest of his life in Europe and espoused antisemitic views during the Second World War. But that is for another column.The Bolshevik thinkers spoke of creating a “New Soviet Man” who was educated, disciplined, rational and committed to collective life. They viewed Chess as a perfect vehicle to create the society they wanted. Chess needed little more than a board, pieces, and two chairs and could be played anywhere. It rewarded study, self-control and contained no element of chance. Chess was also intellectual without being elitist.How the Bolsheviks turned chess into a mass movementIf workers could be taught the game once reserved largely for educated society, chess could become evidence of cultural advancement itself. By the middle of the 1920s, the chess movement had expanded to masses. Chess clubs appeared in factories, and workers' organizations, newspapers and magazines published chess material, and tournaments attracted increasingly large audiences.The Soviet state also tried to convert chess into mass entertainment. In 1924, it organized a public spectacle on the grounds of Leningrad's Palace Square. Sailors and Red Army soldiers became human chess pieces on a giant board, moving across the square before a crowd of spectators.The symbolism would have been difficult to miss.The former Palace Square, the great ceremonial space of imperial Russia, was now hosting chess played by representatives of the revolutionary state.The All-Union chess and checkers congress of 1924 placed chess under the physical culture bureaucracy and put Nikolai Krylenko in charge; 64 was founded the same year with Krylenko as editor. Krylenko was a senior revolutionary who had briefly served as the Bolsheviks’ supreme commander-in-chief in the winter of 1917-18 and later became People's Commissar for Justice.Krylenko had little interest in chess as an elegant diversion.He believed it should serve society. The game, in his conception, formed part of the wider cultural revolution and should contribute to the intellectual education of Soviet citizens.The Soviet state gradually built an ecosystem: chess sections, coaches, tournaments, publications and a ladder through which promising players could rise.From workers’ clubs to a Soviet chess machineThe results of these decades of state support became visible to the world after the Second World War. From Mikhail Botvinnik onward, Soviet players dominated the world championship for decades, barring a brief interlude when Bobby Fischer of America upended Soviet hegemony. Botvinnik, Smyslov, Tal, Petrosian, Spassky, Karpov and Kasparov were very different personalities with very different playing styles, but all emerged from the Soviet state chess system and went on to be counted as among the all-time greats of the game.The Soviet chess machine began during a civil war, when an old Bolshevik chess master, Ilyin-Zhenevsky, persuaded a military bureaucracy that thirty-two wooden pieces on sixty-four squares could help build better revolutionaries.READ ALSO: Italian jobs, French connections and Berlin walls: Chess’s European tourIlyin-Zhenevsky died in a German bombing raid in 1941during the siege of Leningrad. Krylenko, another Bolshevik leader who played a key role, was himself arrested in 1938, sentenced by the Military Collegium, and executed in July 1938. The man who helped build Soviet chess as an instrument of the state was killed by that state.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Joshua Van wins thrilling Alexandre Pantoja rematch after brutal Arman Tsarukyan KO at UFC 331
articles.summary: After dethroning Pantoja in strange circumstances in December, when the Brazilian suffered an early injury, Van sealed a clearer win in their rematch
articles.body:
Joshua Van retained his flyweight title with a thrilling points win over Alexandre Pantoja on Saturday, capping off UFC 331 in Los Angeles.

Van dethroned Pantoja in strange circumstances in December, when the latter suffered an early injury, but the Myanmar native sealed a clearer win in their rematch.

After a typically scintillating start by Pantoja, who took down Van in the opening 10 seconds, the 24-year-old champion began to find the space to execute his fine boxing skills.

As such, the fight seemed to be tied up at 1-1 after the first two rounds, the second of which saw a brief pause while a bloodied Pantoja complained of a headbutt. A replay seemed to show an accidental clash of heads, however.

What ensued was a razor-close third round, in which Pantoja, 36, stacked up more control time and landed plenty of strikes in frantic exchanges, while Van continued to box sharply.

Brazil's Pantoja was dominant with his grappling in round four, leaving the fight seemingly up in the air going into the fifth round, but Van came up clutch.

The champion outstruck Pantoja and even dropped him with a clean right cross late on, before the scorecards all went his way.

They were surprisingly one-sided (49-46, 49-47, 50-45), as Van recorded a second successful title defence, having stopped Tatsuro Taira in an instant classic in May.

In the co-main event, Arman Tsarukyan beat Mauricio Ruffy in what was billed as a lightweight-title eliminator.

The Armenian survived some testing moments – and noticeable damage to his left eye – to stop Ruffy at the end of round one, crumpling him with an elbow against the fence. Tsarukyan, 29, even landed a second elbow as his Brazilian opponent collapsed.

Next for Tsarukyan may be champion Justin Gaethje, who watched from cageside on Saturday.

articles.title: Washington Offense Finds Rhythm In Win Over Eastern Washington
articles.summary: Quickly establishing a rhythm in the pass game was identified earlier in the week as a key indicator of success in Washington’s game against Eastern Washingt...
articles.body:
Quickly establishing a rhythm in the pass game was identified earlier in the week as a key indicator of success in Washington's game against Eastern Washington. The Husky offense did just that in its 48-16 win over the Eagles on Saturday night. Demond Williams began the game 12 of 13 before finishing with 373 passing yards with an 82% completion percentage, four touchdowns, and a pick.

In the first two games of the year, Williams began four of his first eight in the contests against Washington State and Utah State. The offense combined for just three first-quarter points in those games. But on Saturday, Williams opened five for five on the first drive with a passing touchdown to Chris Lawson . He went five for six on the next drive with a passing touchdown to Rashid Williams .

"We were just clicking, coming off the win last week," Rashid Williams said after the game. "We thought that we could be a little bit better, and throughout the whole week, we were just taking it one play at a time."

Those two scoring drives each spanned 70-plus yards and put 14 points on the board in the first quarter alone. Washington had just two 70-plus yard drives against Washington State and Utah State combined.

"This week, you know, we just tried to take our shots," tight end Baron Naone said after the game. "Let the receivers, let the running backs make plays… Make guys miss, [that] was a big thing that we emphasized on this week."

Rashid Williams had the best game of his career against Eastern Washington. He finished with six catches for 86 yards and two touchdowns, and his second score of the day was the most impressive. At the 18-yard line near the end of the second quarter, Demond Williams delivered a back-shoulder pass to Williams, who was well-defended. The 6'-1" receiver extended his left hand as he jumped away from the defender to secure the football with one hand as he fell to the turf.

"I was just seeing that he was pressed," Williams said after the game, describing the catch. "So I just converted the route, gave him a little release, and just looked back a little bit, and D put it in a great spot for me to make a nice catch."

In total, Washington completed passes to nine different receivers in its win over Eastern Washington. Dezmen Roebuck led that group with nine catches for 121 yards, which were both career highs. Of that total, two of Roebuck's receptions were explosive plays for 15-plus yards. He had a long of 43 on the day.

Lawson caught the first touchdown of the game, which was the first receiving score of his career. It was a 15-yard reception to cap off a 74-yard scoring drive. True freshman Jordan Clay had his first career touchdown in the game on a three-yard pass from Williams. Fellow true freshman Mason James had his first statistics, finishing with three catches for 23 yards and three rushing yards.

At tight end, Naone went over 100 receiving yards on just two catches. He had a 28-yard reception and a 75-yard reception for a total of 103 yards in the game. The second of which was on a corner route that he took up the near sideline all the way to the one-yard line.

"Honestly, I was just trying to get into the end zone as fast as I could," Naone said after the game. "I knew he was behind me. Obviously, I didn't think he was that close. I feel like I definitely could have made it in there," he continued. "But, you know, it's all good. We got amazing running backs, amazing scheme, and we punched it in the next play." Ansu Sanoe scored the one-yard touchdown on the very next play to stretch the lead. Sanoe now has two touchdowns on seven carries this season.

While Washington's offense looked efficient against Eastern Washington, there are still some very apparent areas where this team has continued to struggle. The Huskies went to the locker room with 380 yards of offense at the half. Fifty-five of those yards were picked up on a single run by freshman Brian Bonner, who used his track speed to get to the outside for the team's longest run of the year thus far. But if you remove that big play, the Husky running backs averaged just 2.5 yards per carry at the half, and finished the game averaging 3.4 yards per attempt.

Eastern Washington also found success with its quarterback run game against the Husky defense. For the third straight week, Washington's defense allowed at least 60 yards rushing to the opposing quarterback. Nate Bell was able to use misdirection and a slow-mesh read option to break the defensive contain and find big plays to the outside.

On the Eagles' first drive, Bell had runs of 11 and seven yards on back-to-back plays in which the Husky EDGE defenders overran their protection and lost outside contain on the quarterback. Bell later had a 14-yard rushing touchdown and a 32-yard run to the outside, where he again used misdirection to pull the EDGE toward the formation and beat the defense to the outside.

"Hats off to that quarterback," Jedd Fisch said after Bell's performance. "That kid is special. He is elusive, he is hard to bring down, he is fast. And he is accurate, and he's smart." Bell finished with 50 rushing yards, a rushing score, and 150 passing yards.

The offense found its form in the pass game in the Huskies' win over Eastern Washington,, but some things still need to be sorted out. Washington begins Big Ten play next week with Minnesota in town for an 8:00 pm kickoff inside Husky Stadium. After the win over Eastern, Fisch made sure to note that he wants a sellout crowd for the blackout against the Golden Gophers. "We need all of the energy possible to be able to get to 4-0 next week."

articles.title: Stock up, stock down for Northwestern’s 41-7 victory against Colorado
articles.summary: Himon II grabbed for three TDs and Chiles kept building his dual-threat case, but run defense and flags need work.
articles.body:
After a strangely early bye week, Northwestern didn't miss a beat against Colorado on Saturday, burying the Buffaloes by 34 points, riding Joe Himon II's three touchdown catches, Aidan Chiles dominance as a dual-threat quarterback, and a takeaway-heavy defense that led to a lopsided win in the last game held at Martin Stadium.

Himon II could not be stopped Saturday. The graduate student compiled 74 yards against Colorado, with 46 of those coming off three catches. Himon finished the night with three touchdowns, all in the air, including a 25-yard streak where he had nothing but green grass around him. Himon had just 28 yards rushing on four carries, despite running 79 yards for a touchdown, only to be called back for holding.

Simply put, Chiles was incredible in his second-ever game with Northwestern. The transfer did it both in the air and on the ground, throwing for 241 passing yards on 17-for-21 passing (71%) and three passing touchdowns. He was also strong with his legs, picking up two more touchdowns on the ground. Chiles was advertised as a dual-threat quarterback coming into Evanston, and after two games, you certainly can't argue against that.

Northwestern's defense was at it again, forcing some crucial turnovers that led to Wildcat points. The 'Cats forced four turnovers in the first half via two recovered fumbles and an interception, leading to 17 of Northwestern's 41 points. The defense also held strong as Colorado tried every angle to find life, going for it on 4th down three times and getting stopped short each time. Even more impressive, the Buffaloes led the Wildcats in total net yards for much of the game, but turnovers proved to be Colorado's undoing on Saturday.

Honorable Mentions: Red zone efficiency , Griffin Wilde

As much as things went right for the defense, the run defense did not. The 'Cats allowed 180 rushing yards on Saturday. Luckily, a lot of the Wildcat mistakes that allowed for big gains on the ground were undone by Colorado themselves, with two fumbles falling into the hands of a Wildcat, including when the Buffaloes were knocking on the door of a touchdown in the first quarter before LB Braydon Brus scooped it up at the Northwestern 17-yard line.

Despite the lopsided score, Northwestern didn't do itself any favors with the flags. The Wildcats committed eight penalties that gave Colorado an extra 60 yards. The most excruciating came in the first quarter, when Himon ran nearly 80 yards to the end zone and was called back for holding on WR Ricky Ahumaraeze. While not a crucial mistake in the end, it's something to watch moving forward.

For the second game in a row, Northwestern suffered yet another devastating injury on their offensive line. After missing the season debut against South Dakota State due to injury, redshirt sophomore Ezomo Oratokhai exited the game in the first quarter after landing on his ankle. Oratokhai was visibly distraught as he left the field. David Braun said after the game that "we'll know more in the coming days" regarding how it will affect Oratokhai's availability.

Honorable Mentions: The weather, false starts

articles.title: Rookie Salas has walk-off single in 10th as Padres beat Marlins 7-6, reduce magic number to 3
articles.summary: Rookie Ethan Salas singled in Jake Cronenworth from third base with one out in the 10th inning and the San Diego Padres beat the Miami Marlins 7-6 on Saturda...
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO (AP) — Rookie Ethan Salas singled in Jake Cronenworth from third base with one out in the 10th inning and the San Diego Padres beat the Miami Marlins 7-6 on Saturday night to lower their magic number to three for clinching their third straight postseason berth.

Salas, the Padres' top prospect who was called up Sept. 1, punched a single up the middle on an 0-2 pitch from Josh Ekness (2-4) and his teammates mobbed him in a wild celebration that ended up in the outfield.

Cronenworth, the automatic runner, advanced on a wild pitch. David Morgan (4-1) got the victory.

The winning hit came an inning after pinch-hitter Griffin Conine drove a towering, tying homer off Mason Miller with one out in the ninth.

The Padres won for the 12th time in 13 games and remained tied with the Chicago Cubs at 86-69 for the National League's top wild-card spot, although the Cubs hold the tiebreaker. The Philadelphia Phillies lost 10-3 to the New York Mets to drop a game back.

The earliest the Padres can clinch a wild-card spot is Tuesday night at the NL West champion Los Angeles Dodgers .

Miller was trying for a five-out save when Connine hit a 102-mph four-seamer an estimated 427 feet to right, his 17th.

Fernando Tatis Jr. tied it at 5 with a solo homer leading off the fourth off Eury Pérez for the Padres, who on Sunday will go for their second sweep of the Marlins this season.

Ty France then punched an opposite-field double over the outstretched glove of right fielder Esteury Ruiz with two outs in the sixth to bring in Dustin Harris , who was aboard on a one-out opposite field double to left. Harris extended his hitting streak to nine games.

The Marlins roughed up Casey Mize through three innings to take a 5-1 lead, including Otto Lopez 's two-run home run, his 11th, in the second.

San Diego's Samad Taylor homered off Pérez in the second, his second, and the Padres scored three in the third, including on Jake Cronenworth's bases-loaded walk.

Marlins RHP Sandy Alcantara (13-10, 3.85 ERA) and Padres RHP Walker Buehler (8-6, 4.58) were scheduled to start Sunday in the series finale.

articles.title: Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss drops F-bomb on ABC after win over LSU
articles.summary: F-bombs could be heard in the background of the scene in Oxford from the start of College GameDay Saturday morning on ESPN through Saturday night’s ABC broad...
articles.body:
F-bombs could be heard in the background of the scene in Oxford from the start of College GameDay Saturday morning on ESPN through Saturday night's ABC broadcast of the LSU-Ole Miss game. That was Oxford's way of "welcoming" Lane Kiffin back into town.

And even an interview live on ABC shortly after the game produced an F-bomb.

Ole Miss star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss dropped an F-bomb during an interview with ESPN reporter Holly Rowe after No. Ole Miss took down Kiffin and No. 7 LSU 32-24 at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium.

"What is special about this Ole Miss team?" Rowe asked Chambliss during the postgame interview.

"We don't quit," Chambliss explained. "A lot of people may doubt us. They always doubt Ole Miss. I don't know why. We're here now. We're here to compete."

And as Chambliss began to walk off, he looked into the camera and added, "Hotty f*cking Toddy!"

"Wow. Okay," play-by-play announcer Chris Fowler said. "It takes a lot for Trinidad Chambliss to break character like that. But you see the emotion that went into it and came out at the end there."

Chambliss completed 33-of-48 passes for 363 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception, while adding a rushing touchdown in a win that will be remembered for a long time in Oxford. And the Heisman Trophy favorite summarized the feelings of Ole Miss fans with his final comment on ABC.

According to Seth Emerson of The Athletic, Chambliss apologized to Rowe for the F-bomb.

"Which means that in less than a week one-eighth of SEC starting QBs have apologized to Holly Rowe ," Emerson added.

articles.title: Alexey Miranchuk, Lucas Hoyos lead Atlanta United to 1-0 victory over Timbers
articles.summary: Alexey Miranchuk scored in the first half and Lucas Hoyos made it stand up for Atlanta United in a 1-0 victory over the Portland Timbers on Saturday night....
articles.body:
PORTLAND, Ore. (AP) — Alexey Miranchuk scored in the first half and Lucas Hoyos made it stand up for Atlanta United in a 1-0 victory over the Portland Timbers on Saturday night.

Miranchuk used assists from Miguel Almirón and Júnior Alonso to score his sixth goal this season and give Atlanta United (7-14-5) the lead in the 28th minute. Miranchuk finished with six goals in 33 appearances last year in his first full season in the league.

Hoyos had three saves for Atlanta United, now 4-2-2 in its last eight matches. It was the 37-year-old's third shutout in his first 26 starts after joining the club in the offseason.

James Pantemis stopped two shots for Portland (9-12-5), which is clinging to the ninth and final playoff spot in the Western Conference.

The Timbers have lost two straight and scored four goals in three matches since beating Minnesota United 5-4 at home to start the month.

Portland drops to 7-4-3 at home, while Atlanta United improves to 3-7-4 on the road.

Atlanta: Hosts New York City FC on Saturday.

Portland: At San Jose Earthquakes on Saturday.

articles.title: Two months after getting cut, Pavin Smith's game-ending homer gives D-backs playoff hope
articles.summary: Torey Lovullo has said the same phrase several times over the past seven years, even as fans and sometimes reporters rolled their eyes at the Arizona Diamond...
articles.body:
PHOENIX (AP) — Torey Lovullo has said the same phrase several times over the past seven years, even as fans and sometimes reporters rolled their eyes at the Arizona Diamondbacks manager's optimism.

" Pavin Smith can hit," Lovullo would say.

And on Saturday night, he finally did, injecting some life into the D-backs' slim playoff hopes by smacking a game-ending, two-run homer in the ninth inning for a 5-3 win over the New York Yankees . Entering as a pinch-hitter, the left-hander ripped a cutter from Michael Fulmer over the right-field wall.

The D-backs pulled within four games of Philadelphia for the final NL wild card with seven games remaining.

"I'm never looking to be proven right," Lovullo said. "I'm just trying to put players in the best position to be successful and when they have success I share it with them. But I do believe Pavin can hit."

Smith has had an up-and-down career with the D-backs after being selected with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2017 amateur draft after a stellar three seasons in college at Virginia. He has a career batting average of .241 with 47 homers, but has been worth exactly 0.0 wins above replacement, according to baseball-reference.com .

The 30-year-old looked like he might finally be ready for his breakout season this spring, but he developed bone spurs in his elbow in March and needed surgery. That knocked him out of action for roughly two months.

He returned to the lineup on June 1, but looked lost at the plate. The low point came on July 9 when he was designated for assignment by the only organization he had ever known. At the time, he was hitting .141.

Smith cleared waivers, meaning 29 other teams didn't think he was worth picking up. Then the D-backs sent him back to Triple-A Reno, where he slowly regained confidence in his swing.

Now he's making big contributions at a critical stage of the season.

"It felt really good," Smith said. "There were lots of times this year when I didn't feel like I could ever hit again. I think that happens to a lot of people. Just didn't have any timing coming back from the surgery."

Smith's homer was a crowd-pleaser at Chase Field, where a season-high 47,918 fans were in attendance for the franchise's 25-year anniversary celebration of their 2001 World Series win over the Yankees.

Lovullo said their might have been a little magic in the air for the D-backs since so many franchise legends were in the building, including Luis Gonzalez, whose bloop single off Yankees closer and Hall of Famer Mariano Rivera in the ninth inning of Game 7 scored Jay Bell for a 3-2 win.

"Gonzo hit a walk-off about 25 years ago and to be able to do it on the (celebration) night is pretty cool," Smith said. "It's a full stadium. It was a playoff-like atmosphere. Every pitch felt like it mattered more and to pull it out in the end feels good."
